chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fasting person, does he smell the basil or not? Do you see that permissible for him? He said: There is no objection.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does smelling basil break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh ruling on whether smelling basil (*rihan*) invalidates the fast, affirming that it is permissible (*la ba'sa*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between mere olfaction and the ingestion of substantial particles, reinforcing the principle that the fast is only broken by eating, drinking, or sexual intercourse. The transmission chain through Safwan and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly tradition in preserving these practical legal details.
